root_cause.text: In i915's shmem_sg_alloc_table(), folio-backed pages were coalesced into a single scatterlist entry without enforcing the scatterlist's unsigned int length/max_segment limit, allowing sg->length to overflow at 4GB+ object sizes.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly says the scatterlist unsigned int .length "may get overflowed" when folio pages for 4GB+ GEM shmem objects are added to one scatterlist, and the patch fixes this by capping nr_pages with max_segment / PAGE_SIZE and with (max_segment - sg->length) / PAGE_SIZE before doing sg->length += nr_pages * PAGE_SIZE; it also replaces the prior comment "/* XXX: could overflow? */".

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In i915's shmem_sg_alloc_table(), folio-backed pages were coalesced into a single scatterlist entry without enforcing the scatterlist's unsigned int length/max_segment limit, allowing sg->length to overflow at 4GB+ object sizes.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message explicitly says the scatterlist unsigned int .length "may get overflowed" when folio pages for 4GB+ GEM shmem objects are added to one scatterlist, and the patch fixes this by capping nr_pages with max_segment / PAGE_SIZE and with (max_segment - sg->length) / PAGE_SIZE before doing sg->length += nr_pages * PAGE_SIZE; it also replaces the prior comment "/* XXX: could overflow? */".

intent_record.intent_summary: Limit `nr_pages` by the maximum segment size in pages so shmem scatterlist segments do not exceed `max_segment`.
intent_record.what: The two-line assignment of `nr_pages` using `min_t(unsigned long, folio_nr_pages(folio), page_count - i)` was replaced with a `min_array` call over three `unsigned long` values: `folio_nr_pages(folio)`, `page_count - i`, and `max_segment / PAGE_SIZE`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the number of pages assigned to `nr_pages` is now additionally capped by the maximum segment size expressed in pages, preventing a scatterlist chunk from spanning more pages than `max_segment` allows even when the folio and remaining page count are larger.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clamp merged scatter-gather page counts so segment length never grows past `max_segment` when extending an existing entry.
intent_record.what: The change replaces a comment in the scatter-gather merge path with an assignment that clamps `nr_pages` using `min_t(unsigned long, nr_pages, (max_segment - sg->length) / PAGE_SIZE)` before adding `nr_pages * PAGE_SIZE` to `sg->length`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents extending an existing scatter-gather segment beyond `max_segment` when contiguous folios are merged, ensuring the added length is limited to the remaining allowed bytes in the current segment and avoiding oversized segment lengths or related overflow/limit violations.

grouping_result.intent: Clamp merged scatter-gather page counts so segment length never grows past `max_segment` when extending an existing entry.

consistency_review.core_intent: Clamp scatter-gather segment page counts during shmem entry creation and extension so merged segments never exceed max_segment.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly enforce the scatterlist max_segment limit when creating and extending shmem scatterlist entries, which addresses the root cause of folio-backed pages being coalesced into oversized sg entries and overflowing sg->length.

candidates.rationale: This is the direct overflow point: when coalescing folio-backed pages into an existing scatterlist entry, the code increases sg->length without enforcing the unsigned int/max_segment bound, allowing wraparound for 4GB+ merged segments.

This boundary check is insufficient by itself because it only checks the current length before extension, not whether adding nr_pages * PAGE_SIZE will exceed max_segment. That logic enables oversized merged segments.

Before the fix, nr_pages was limited only by folio size and remaining page_count, not by max_segment. This allowed creation or extension of entries with too many pages for a single scatterlist segment.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the direct vulnerable statement. It extends an existing scatterlist entry by adding folio-backed pages without checking whether the resulting segment length exceeds the scatterlist unsigned int/max_segment limit, allowing sg->length to overflow for 4GB+ merged segments.

This pre-extension guard is insufficient because it only tests the current segment length, not whether adding nr_pages * PAGE_SIZE will push the segment past max_segment. That flawed condition permits oversized merged segments to reach the overflowing increment.

This computation was part of the root cause because nr_pages was not constrained by the maximum segment size before being used to create or extend a scatterlist entry. As a result, too many pages could be coalesced into one segment, enabling the later length overflow.

i915: Limit the length of an sg list to the requested length

The folio conversion changed the behaviour of shmem_sg_all
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 26a8e32e6d77900819c0c730fbfb393692dbbeea
Author: Matthew Wilcox (Oracle) <willy@infradead.org>
Date:   Tue Sep 19 20:48:55 2023 +0100

    i915: Limit the length of an sg list to the requested length
    
    The folio conversion changed the behaviour of shmem_sg_alloc_table() to
    put the entire length of the last folio into the sg list, even if the sg
    list should have been shorter.  gen8_ggtt_insert_entries() relied on the
    list being the right length and would overrun the end
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the exact scatterlist length construction logic in shmem_sg_alloc_table(). The vulnerable behavior described in the root cause was coalescing folio-backed pages using the full folio size without clamping to the remaining requested object length. In this commit, that handling is explicitly corrected by introducing `nr_pages = min_t(unsigned long, folio_nr_pages(folio), page_count - i);`, which limits each folio contribution to the remaining number of pages requested. The scatterlist entry is then created with `sg_set_folio(sg, folio, nr_pages * PAGE_SIZE, 0);` instead of `folio_size(folio)`, and coalescing uses `sg->length += nr_pages * PAGE_SIZE;` instead of `folio_size(folio)`. The traversal state is also updated consistently with `next_pfn = folio_pfn(folio) + nr_pages;` and `i += nr_pages - 1;`. These lines show the last folio is clamped to the requested length, which is the fix described by the commit message. Therefore the vulnerable construct is not present in this version, and the fix is present.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is clearly present in `shmem_get_pages()`. The function coalesces contiguous pages into a single scatterlist entry using `else { sg->length += PAGE_SIZE; }`. The only limit checked before extending an entry is `sg->length >= max_segment` in the condition `if (!i || sg->length >= max_segment || page_to_pfn(page) != last_pfn + 1)`. This is insufficient for preventing overflow because it checks the current length before increment, not whether `sg->length + PAGE_SIZE` would exceed either `max_segment` or the scatterlist `unsigned int` length capacity. As a result, for large folio/contiguous page runs, `sg->length` can grow past the representable/allowed limit, matching the root cause that folio-backed pages were coalesced without enforcing the scatterlist length/max_segment limit. There is no protective check such as `sg->length > max_segment - PAGE_SIZE` or equivalent overflow-safe bound, so the fix is not present.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 26a8e32e6d77900819c0c730fbfb393692dbbeea
Author: Matthew Wilcox (Oracle) <willy@infradead.org>
Date:   Tue Sep 19 20:48:55 2023 +0100

    i915: Limit the length of an sg list to the requested length
    
    The folio conversion changed the behaviour of shmem_sg_alloc_table() to
    put the entire length of the last folio into the sg list, even if the sg
    list should have been shorter.  gen8_ggtt_insert_entries() relied on the
    list being the right length and would overrun the end
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the exact scatterlist coalescing logic in shmem_sg_alloc_table(). The root cause described is failure to enforce the scatterlist unsigned-int length / max_segment limit when coalescing folio-backed pages. In this commit, the code adds a clamp for the requested object length via `nr_pages = min_t(unsigned long, folio_nr_pages(folio), page_count - i);` and then uses `nr_pages * PAGE_SIZE` in `sg_set_folio()` and `sg->length += nr_pages * PAGE_SIZE;`, which fixes the 'last folio extends past requested length' issue from the commit message. However, the vulnerable construct is still present with respect to max_segment enforcement during coalescing: the branch condition is `if (!i || sg->length >= max_segment || folio_pfn(folio) != next_pfn)`, and in the coalescing path it does `sg->length += nr_pages * PAGE_SIZE;` with the explicit comment `/* XXX: could overflow? */`. This checks only whether the current `sg->length` is already `>= max_segment` before appending, but does not check whether `sg->length + nr_pages * PAGE_SIZE` would exceed `max_segment` or overflow the unsigned int length field. Therefore the buggy construct remains present, and the full fix for the described overflow vulnerability is not yet in this function.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant logic is fully present in `shmem_get_pages()`, so the snippet is sufficient. The vulnerable construct appears in the scatterlist coalescing loop: `if (!i || sg->length >= max_segment || page_to_pfn(page) != last_pfn + 1) { ... sg_set_page(sg, page, PAGE_SIZE, 0); } else { sg->length += PAGE_SIZE; }`. This code merges contiguous pages by directly increasing `sg->length` with `sg->length += PAGE_SIZE`, but it only checks `sg->length >= max_segment` before extending, not whether adding another page would exceed either `max_segment` or the scatterlist `unsigned int` length limit. As a result, when `sg->length` is below the limit but close to it, the addition can overflow or exceed the allowed segment size, matching the root cause: folio-backed/contiguous pages are coalesced without enforcing the maximum length bound during the append step. No fix is present here, because there is no guard such as checking `sg->length + PAGE_SIZE > max_segment` or otherwise preventing `sg->length` overflow before incrementing.
